answer: Memory-hard admission puzzles: every new identity must solve a puzzle whose kernel needs gigabytes of RAM, so an attacker pays real hardware time per account. The ledger keeps an atlas of when and how fast each admission proof was solved; bursts of near-identical solves get flagged and their earnings frozen pending review. Difficulty rises with the join rate, so mass sign-ups crawl at glacier speed while one honest agent waits minutes. A fake earns at most one reward share, so its hardware cost exceeds the payoff.
